title: Ella Langley, Adéla, Beyoncé & More: Highlights of This Week’s Billboard Charts
summary: All of Billboard’s charts update each Tuesday.
contentText:
Tuesday is new Billboard chart day each week! As all charts update each Tuesday morning, here’s a look at highlights of the latest rankings, dated Sept. 19 and reflecting the Sept. 4-10 measurement week, according to data tracker Luminate.

Among this week’s chart stars are Ella Langley , Adéla, Beyoncé, Karol G and … The Simpsons .

As previously reported , Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas” scores a 22nd week at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — tying for the most time spent atop the chart, as it equals Mariah Carey’s merry No. 1 run with “All I Want for Christmas Is You.”

Related

Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Ties All-Time Hot 100 Record With 22nd Week at No. 1

Plus, “Choosin’ Texas” parent album Dandelion rebounds for a third week at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 , while the set becomes the first by a woman this decade to spin off four top 10s on the Country Airplay chart. “Loving Life Again” rises to No. 8 on Country Airplay, after “Choosin’ Texas,” “Be Her” and Langley’s Morgan Wallen duet “I Can’t Love You Anymore” each led the list.

The album with the most Country Airplay top 10s among all artists? Shania Twain sent eight classics to the tier from Come On Over in 1997-99: the No. 1s “Love Gets Me Every Time,” “You’re Still the One” and “Honey, I’m Home”; the No. 4-peaking “Man! I Feel Like a Woman!”; the No. 6 hits “Don’t Be Stupid (You Know I Love You)”; “From This Moment On,” with Bryan White and the title track; and the No. 8-reaching “That Don’t Impress Me Much.”

Meanwhile, Come On Over ruled Top Country Albums for 50 weeks through 2000, the most for an album by a woman.

Check out more key highlights from this week’s Billboard charts below — including a new song that updates Twain’s breakthrough hit.
